CoronarySAM2: click an artery, get a mask

A tool that segments coronary arteries in X-ray angiography. You click on the vessel, SAM2 proposes a mask, and you add include or exclude points until it is right.

The problem

Outlining coronary arteries by hand on an angiogram is slow, and fully automatic models miss thin branches with no way to correct them. A promptable model fits better, because the person looking at the image can point at what they mean.

I fine-tuned SAM2 on coronary angiograms so that a few clicks give a usable mask, then packaged it as a browser demo anyone can try. The page you are reading explains the model. It is a research and education tool and is not cleared for clinical use.

How it works

  1. Clean the image.Gaussian-blur intensity normalization, then CLAHE contrast enhancement (clip limit 2.0, 8x8 tiles), then a resize to 1024x1024 RGB.
  2. Encode once.SAM2's Hiera image encoder turns the image into features. One script keeps it frozen, another also trains part of it.
  3. Click.Positive and negative points become prompt embeddings. Click again to refine.
  4. Decode a mask.The mask decoder combines features and prompts into a mask, drawn over your image.

Source: evaluation_results.csv, written by SAM2_Evaluation_pipeline.py. The row is the Tiny checkpoint at epoch 5, with 5 points per image sampled from the ground-truth mask.

Pixel accuracy is high mostly because most pixels are background. Dice and IoU are the numbers to read.

Limits and next steps

  • One checkpoint is evaluated, and the repo has no comparison table for the other three sizes. The model card ranks them qualitatively, which is not a measurement.
  • The evaluation prompts come from the ground-truth mask. A person clicking by hand will place points differently, so real use can score lower.
  • The data directory name says it is an augmented set. The repo does not show whether augmented copies of one image can land in both the training and test split, so I read 0.83 as an upper bound until I check.
  • The model card lists known weak spots: thin branches, heavy vessel overlap, low-quality frames. It is for research only and not cleared for diagnosis.

Fine-tuning scripts train the prompt encoder and mask decoder with the image encoder frozen. A second script also trains the image encoder in a separate parameter group.
